audit_findings.title: The cash bridge includes assets economically owned by noncontrolling interests
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; $389.2 million of the $637.667 million cash-and-investments bridge was held by joint ventures, while total noncontrolling-interest equity was $452.211 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds consolidated cash to equity value attributable only to PLAB common shares without deducting the minority owners' economic share.
audit_findings.evidence: As of October 31, 2025, total cash and cash equivalents included $446.1 million held by foreign subsidiaries, including an aggregate of $353.8 million held by our joint ventures in Taiwan and China.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated claim-perimeter error, although the cash-specific adjustment is unresolved. Joint-venture cash equals 61.0% of bridge cash and 34.5% of the $1.128 billion base equity value, so the minority-owned portion is reasonably capable of materially reducing value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the May 3, 2026 cash and short-term-investment balances by legal entity, apply each entity's ownership percentages, and rerun all scenarios using only PLAB's economic share or an explicit NCI claim deduction.

audit_findings.title: Owner earnings mix a parent numerator with consolidated cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2025 consolidated depreciation and amortization was $77.258 million, capital expenditures were $188.137 million, and NCI income was $53.829 million versus the $34.9 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable net income is combined with consolidated depreciation, capital expenditures, and working-capital changes to form owner earnings applied to the parent-only share count.
audit_findings.evidence: The results of noncontrolling ownership interests held by Photronics, net of tax, are reported as Net (income) attributable to noncontrolling interests in the consolidated statements of income.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim mismatch is demonstrated, but its net direction and amount cannot be established without subsidiary cash-flow allocations. The mismatched depreciation and capital-expenditure amounts are each large relative to the anchor, making a material change to operating value reasonably possible.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every historical OE year on one consistent perimeter: either consolidated OE less NCI-attributable free cash flow or parent-attributable earnings plus only PLAB's economic share of each cash-flow adjustment; then recompute the anchor, trend, scenarios, and per-share values.

audit_findings.title: Material noncash tax releases may remain in the FY2025 anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $19.551 million of filed tax releases—$16.751 million valuation-allowance release plus $2.8 million uncertain-tax-position reversals—equal to 56.0% of the $34.9 million anchor; the amount retained in OE is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retained noncash, nonrecurring tax benefit increases anchor OE and is then capitalized through forecast growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The effective income tax rate decreased in Q4 FY25 compared with Q3 FY25 primarily due to the release of a $16.7 million valuation allowance related to deferred tax assets that are now expected to be realized in future periods, as well as $2.8 million of reversals of uncertain tax positions mainly resulting from audit settlements and statute expirations.
audit_findings.explanation: The tax benefits are demonstrated, including the $16.751 million parent-income adjustment disclosed in the company's non-GAAP reconciliation. Whether the OE worksheet already removed them is unresolved. If substantially retained, their scale relative to the anchor is plainly material.
audit_findings.action: Trace both releases through parent-attributable income and every FY2025 OE adjustment, remove only the portions that increased OE without recurring cash availability, and rerun the anchor and all valuation scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Cash treated as excess may be required for the imminent capital program
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; $211.3 million of committed and recognized capital obligations existed at May 3, 2026, with $199.0 million expected within twelve months, against a $330 million FY2026 capital-expenditure forecast
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge treats all $637.667 million of cash and investments as distributable while forecast OE grows a FY2025 anchor containing only $188.137 million of capital expenditures and no explicit FY2026 step-up.
audit_findings.evidence: Our capital expenditure payments for fiscal 2026 are expected to be approximately $330 million, of which approximately $13.0 million was included in Accounts payable and Accrued liabilities on our October 31, 2025 consolidated balance sheet.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligations are current filed amounts, not merely a general future risk. The $211.3 million obligation equals 18.7% of base equity value, but it cannot all automatically be deducted because operating cash flow may fund part of it and expansion spending may create future earnings. The unresolved double-counting remains reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2026 spending paid to date, remaining commitments, maintenance versus expansion capital, expected operating funding, and minimum local cash reserves; then rerun OE with the actual outlay schedule or exclude committed and operating cash from the bridge without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Foreign cash is added at face value despite unquantified repatriation leakage
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; $464.9 million of cash was held by foreign subsidiaries at May 3, 2026, including $389.2 million at joint ventures
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds foreign cash dollar-for-dollar even though withholding taxes, state taxes, transfer procedures, restrictions, and local operating requirements may reduce its realizable value to the parent.
audit_findings.evidence: Therefore, should we elect in the future to repatriate the remaining foreign earnings deemed to be indefinitely reinvested, we may incur additional state and foreign withholding tax expense on those earnings, the amount of which is not practicable to compute.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing confirms possible tax leakage and says its amount is not practicable to compute. The exposed balance is large, but the record supplies neither applicable extraction rates nor the portion intended for repatriation; therefore materiality cannot presently be established. This issue applies after separately correcting for NCI ownership.
audit_findings.action: Map cash and investments by entity and jurisdiction, isolate PLAB's economic share, model realistic dividend or liquidation routes with withholding and state taxes, identify restricted and permanently reinvested balances, and rerun the bridge at estimated net realizable value.
